_note: Verified fact sheets for the safari re-author (Oct 2026). Built from the Gemini Flash audit plus Claude web research; every season window below was checked against at least one operator or park source. Passed to Gemini as ground truth; mustMention is only a post-check.

kruger.scope: Kruger National Park (self-drive on public roads plus guided drives) and the unfenced private reserves along its western edge, above all Sabi Sands, where off-road tracking gives the best leopard sightings.
facts: Dry season runs roughly May to October; vegetation thins and animals concentrate at the rivers and dams (Sabie, Olifants).
June to August is the sweet spot: cool, open bush. September and October are the peak of concentration at remaining water but the days get hot.
Rains run about November to April: hot, humid, thick bush that hides animals, but impala lambing and baby animals from November to December and the best birding with migrants.
The Big Five are all resident year-round, but seeing all five in one trip is not guaranteed.
Kruger is a malaria area, most risk in the wet summer months.
avoid: Saying September or October is when sightings ease or vegetation thickens: October is still dry and productive; thick bush returns with the November rains.
kruger.season: Peak June to October (September and October best for concentration); lowest January to March.

kenya.scope: Maasai Mara (Mara River crossings, big cats) and Amboseli (elephants with Kilimanjaro behind them).
facts: The Great Migration herds arrive in the Mara from the Serengeti around July and leave by late October; river crossings are most likely August and September, with the first from about mid-July and again as herds return in October.
The long rains (April and May) are the low season: heavy rain damages roads, many camps and lodges close, grass is tall, vehicles are few.
The short rains (October and November) do not seriously disrupt game viewing.
January and February are the short dry season with excellent visibility and resident big cats and elephants.
Amboseli's elephant herds against Kilimanjaro are a draw independent of the migration; best in the dry months.
avoid: Scoring or describing March to May as 'excellent, just muddier': April and May are the weakest months of the year.
kenya.season: Peak July to October (August and September highest); strong January and February and December; weakest April and May.

tanzania.scope: Serengeti ecosystem only (the southern plains around Ndutu and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, the western corridor, and the northern Serengeti around Kogatende); Zanzibar is a beach extension, not a safari.
facts: Calving on the short-grass plains around Ndutu runs from late January through March, peaking in February, with more than half a million calves and heavy predator activity.
The herds drift north and west through the western corridor from April to June, with Grumeti River crossings around June.
Mara River crossings in the northern Serengeti (Kogatende) run roughly July to October, peaking August and September; herds head back south from late October.
The long rains (April and May) are the low season: green, cheaper, few vehicles, some heavy rain, herds mid-migration.
The short rains in November bring fresh grass as herds return south.
avoid: Saying crossings are past their peak in September: August and September are the peak.
Scoring every month except April and May at 10.
tanzania.season: Peak January to March (calving) and July to October (crossings, August and September highest); lower April, May and November; early June and December in between.

botswana.scope: Okavango Delta and Moremi Game Reserve for land and water safaris (mokoro canoe, boat, game drive), with the Chobe riverfront for elephant herds.
facts: Floodwater from Angola's summer rains takes about four months to arrive, entering the Delta between March and May, peaking around June and July in Moremi (about mid-August around Maun), then receding.
Best game viewing is roughly July to October: flooded channels (water safaris) alongside a dry landscape, with animals concentrated on the remaining dry ground.
October is the hottest month, often above 40 C, with excellent waterhole and channel-edge viewing.
The green season (November to March) brings rain, thick bush, newborn animals, predators working them, and strong birding; some camps are closed and mokoro trips are limited in seasonal areas.
Wild dogs den around June to August and are easier to find then.
avoid: Saying the Delta's water is at its lowest in October: it recedes from about September; the lowest levels come around December to March before the next flood.
botswana.season: Peak July to October; strong May, June, November; lowest January to March.

zambia.scope: South Luangwa National Park and the Luangwa River.
facts: Birthplace of the walking safari (Norman Carr, 1950s); known as the Valley of the Leopard for one of Africa's highest leopard densities, with night drives allowed.
Dry season June to October is the peak; game packs along the river and shrinking lagoons, and predator action intensifies in September and October.

Many remote walking camps are open only from about April or May to November; the wet season (December to March) brings thick green bush, flooded tracks and most camps closed, with a few offering boat safaris and birding.
Southern Carmine Bee-eaters nest in colonies in the riverbanks in the late dry season (about August to November).
Thornicroft's giraffe is found only in the Luangwa Valley.
avoid: Scoring October below July: October is among the best months.
zambia.season: Peak July to October; strong May and June and November shoulder; lowest January to March.

zimbabwe.scope: Hwange National Park, with Victoria Falls as the gateway.
facts: Hwange has almost no natural surface water; its 45,000 or more elephants depend on pumped waterholes, which draw very large herds in the dry season, with lions and other predators close behind.
August to early November is the best game viewing; September is often the strongest and October is hot with excellent elephant sightings.
Hwange holds one of the largest African wild dog populations, with wild dogs and cheetah hunting the open vleis.
The park begins roughly an hour south of Victoria Falls; main camps are one to three hours farther depending on the camp.
The wet season (about November to March) disperses game away from the pumped waterholes.
avoid: Treating the Victoria Falls themselves as safari content.
zimbabwe.season: Peak August to October; strong June, July and November; lowest January to March.

namibia.scope: Etosha National Park (the main safari), with a mention of the Zambezi Region's riverside elephant safaris and Damaraland's desert-adapted elephant tracking only if space allows.
facts: Dry season June to October is the best; animals gather at waterholes along the southern edge of the Etosha Pan.
Okaukuejo's floodlit waterhole draws black rhino and elephant at night; Halali's draws leopard; Namutoni has fewer big game but strong birding.
September and October are the hottest months and the best for waterhole concentration; October is still peak, not easing.
Rains begin about November and run to April: game disperses, the park is green, birding is at its best with migrants.
avoid: Saying October is when waterhole concentration eases: that begins with the November rains.
namibia.season: Peak July to October (September and October highest); lowest January to March.

uganda.scope: Murchison Falls National Park (Nile boat trip, savanna game drives) and Queen Elizabeth National Park (Kazinga Channel boat cruise, Ishasha tree-climbing lions). Gorilla trekking is NOT safari and stays out.
facts: Murchison Falls: elephants, giraffes, lions, buffalo and hippos on game drives north of the Nile, plus the boat trip to the base of the falls; best months December to February and June to September.

Queen Elizabeth: elephants, lions, buffalo and abundant hippos; the Kazinga Channel boat cruise brings hippos, crocodiles and buffalo close; the Ishasha sector is famous for lions that climb fig trees.
Dry seasons are roughly December to February and June to September; the rains (about March to May and October to November) make some tracks muddy.
Rhinos are not in these parks (they are in a separate sanctuary), so Uganda is not a Big Five destination.
avoid: Any gorilla or chimpanzee trekking content.
uganda.season: Peak December to February and June to August; lowest April, May and November.

rwanda.scope: Akagera National Park only (Rwanda's only savanna park). Gorilla trekking at Volcanoes is NOT safari and stays out.
facts: Seven lions were reintroduced in 2015 after about twenty years without them, and the population has grown strongly since; eastern black rhinos returned in 2017 and white rhinos were added in 2021, so all Big Five are present again.
Boat trips on Lake Ihema show hippos, crocodiles and waterbirds.
June to September is the long dry season and best for game viewing; the shorter dry spell is about December to February; heavier rain falls about March to May and October to November.
rwanda.season: Peak June to September; moderate December to February; lowest April and May.

ethiopia.scope: Real but modest game viewing in Awash National Park, Nechisar National Park, and the remote Omo and Mago parks; game numbers are far lower and access harder than East Africa. Simien and Bale trekking is NOT safari and stays out.
facts: Awash National Park, about 225 km east of Addis Ababa: beisa oryx, greater and lesser kudu, Soemmerring's gazelle, Swayne's hartebeest, hot springs and volcanic terrain; open year-round, best roughly September to November.
Nechisar National Park (near Arba Minch): zebra, Grant's gazelle and Swayne's hartebeest on the plains, and boat trips on Lake Chamo to see large crocodiles; best roughly November to March.

Omo and Mago National Parks in the far south are the last places in Ethiopia with elephant, buffalo, giraffe, eland and big cats, but they are remote; best January and February, and roads become nearly impassable after rain (April, May and October).
Gambella in the far west sits on the northern edge of the white-eared kob migration and is very remote.
avoid: Gelada, Walia ibex or Ethiopian wolf content (wildlife section).
ethiopia.season: Low overall; best roughly November to March, with Awash good from September; lowest during the rains (about April to May and June to August).

ghana.scope: Mole National Park in the northwest.
facts: Mole offers both walking safaris with armed rangers and vehicle game drives (including night drives); it is not either-or.
Elephants are the highlight and are seen most easily December to March, when the dry season concentrates them at waterholes and the dam near the park lodging.
The park is about three hours by road from Tamale, which has flights from Accra; the dry season is roughly November to April.
Game numbers are modest compared with East or southern Africa.
ghana.season: Peak December to March; the rains (about May to October) are the low season.

nepal.scope: Chitwan National Park (with Bardia National Park in the far west as the quieter alternative).
facts: Greater one-horned rhinos are seen on most safaris; the park holds about 700 of them. Tigers are present but a sighting is a lucky event, not routine.

Jeep safaris inside the park are suspended for the monsoon from about the end of June to mid-September; walking and canoe trips in the buffer zone and along the river continue in some form, so the park is not entirely closed.

October to March is the main dry season with the best visibility; March to May is hot, the grass is short, and animals are drawn to water; some operators call October to December the best window for tigers.
Gharial crocodiles are seen on river trips.
avoid: Saying the park closes entirely for the monsoon.
Quoting a precise daily tiger percentage.
nepal.season: Peak October to March; reasonable April and May despite heat; lowest July to September.

facts: The park holds about two-thirds of the world's greater one-horned rhinos, plus wild elephants, wild water buffalo, swamp deer and a growing tiger population (136 tigers in the 2022 count).

It is closed each year from about May to October because the Brahmaputra floods most of the park; the reopening date varies year to year, announced anywhere from about October 1 to late October, so the main season is November to April.
Jeep safaris run in the Kohora (central), Bagori (western), Burapahar and Agoratoli ranges; elephant-back rides at dawn run from Kohora and Bagori.
Tall elephant grass dries in December and January and is then burned by park staff, opening up sightlines through about March.
avoid: Saying grass burning is mainly February to April.
kaziranga.season: Peak December to March; good November and April; closed May to September (score near zero); October depends on the reopening date.

rajasthan-golden-triangle.scope: Ranthambore National Park for tigers (the standard safari add-on to the Golden Triangle).
facts: The park is open roughly October 1 to June 30; core zones 1 to 5 close from July to September for the monsoon, while buffer zones 6 to 10 stay open with much lower tiger odds.
The best tiger sightings come in the dry run-up to the monsoon, April to June, when tigers visit lakes and waterholes in the heat; sightings are never guaranteed.
Leopards and sloth bears are occasional; winter mornings are cold in open jeeps.
Ranthambore is about 165 to 200 km from Jaipur, roughly three and a half hours by road.
rajasthan-golden-triangle.season: Peak April to June; good October to March; core zones closed July to September (score near zero).

srilanka.scope: Minneriya and Kaudulla (the elephant Gathering), Yala (leopards), Udawalawe (elephants year-round), with Wilpattu as the quieter option.
facts: The Gathering of up to 200 to 300 wild Asian elephants at Minneriya Tank runs roughly July to October, peaking August and September; Kaudulla takes over or shares the herds at different times.
Yala holds one of the highest leopard densities in the world; February to June or July is the best window for leopards and sloth bears.
Udawalawe has more than 500 resident elephants and good sightings through the year.
Wilpattu is best roughly February to October for leopards and sloth bears.
Minneriya is about 30 to 60 minutes from the Sigiriya and Dambulla hub.
avoid: Calling May and June the driest, quietest stretch at Minneriya.
srilanka.season: Peak August and September (Gathering); strong February to July for Yala; lowest during the northeast monsoon rains of about November to January.

pantanal.scope: The northern Pantanal around Porto Jofre at the end of the Transpantaneira road (boat-based jaguar safaris).
facts: June to October is the dry season and jaguar season; July to early October has the most sightings, August and September are ideal, and multi-day boat safaris report success rates above 90 percent.
The Transpantaneira is a dirt road of more than 100 bridges running about 147 km from Poconé to Porto Jofre; the gateway city is Cuiabá.
The rainy season (about November to March) floods the plains: roads can be impassable, some lodges become boat-access only, and wildlife disperses.
Giant river otters, caimans and capybaras are seen on the same boat trips; giant anteaters and hyacinth macaws are better in the southern Pantanal.
avoid: Saying jaguar odds are already improving in April: water is still high until about June.
pantanal.season: Peak July to October (August and September highest); transitional May and June and November; lowest January to March.

borneo.scope: The Kinabatangan River (small-boat river safaris), with Danum Valley and Tabin Wildlife Reserve as land-based alternatives in Sabah.
facts: River cruises at dawn and dusk show orangutans, proboscis monkeys, hornbills and macaques; pygmy elephants are less predictable, appearing on a fraction of trips.

The dry season is roughly March to September (peak May to September), when animals gather at the river; October to February is wetter and the river runs higher, though wildlife still concentrates along the corridor.
Tabin Wildlife Reserve is known for pygmy elephants and banteng; Danum Valley for orangutans and, rarely, clouded leopard.
avoid: Calling the whole year equally low-scoring.
borneo.season: Peak May to September; good March, April and October; lowest December and January.
